Explain that the room location listed in the confirmation email is incorrect.
Ask for the correct room location before the class starts in two days.

academicDiscussion.professorPost: Many city tree-planting programs are debating whether to require native species exclusively. Native trees tend to support local insects, birds, and soil organisms more effectively than imported species, but they often grow more slowly than some non-native trees that can provide usable shade within just a few years. Should city planting programs require native species only, even if it means residents wait longer for shade? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Priya
studentPosts.post: I think cities should require native species only. Non-native trees might shade a street faster, but they rarely support local birds or insects the way native trees do. If we keep choosing quick fixes, we lose the long-term ecological value these programs are supposed to protect for the whole neighborhood.

studentPosts.name: Marcus
studentPosts.post: I get Priya's point about biodiversity, but people live with heat right now. A neighborhood without real shade for ten years while a native oak slowly matures isn't a fair trade for residents dealing with rising summer temperatures. Programs should mix both species types instead of picking only one.
